name: Fairshake

summary.text: Fairshake is a U.S. super PAC funded mainly by cryptocurrency companies and investors, including Coinbase, Ripple and Andreessen Horowitz. Together with its affiliates Protect Progress and Defend American Jobs, it spent roughly $195 million in the 2024 cycle supporting pro-crypto congressional candidates and opposing others. It reported a $193 million war chest at the end of 2025 ahead of the 2026 midterms.

sources.title: Crypto PAC Fairshake touts $193 million war chest as regulatory bill faces first vote
How tech bros bought 'America's most pro-crypto Congress ever'

facts.claim: In 2024, crypto industry PACs directed about $40 million at defeating Senate Banking Committee Chair Sherrod Brown in Ohio, largely through Fairshake's affiliate Defend American Jobs. Fairshake itself spent over $10 million on ads against Rep. Katie Porter in California's Senate primary.

sources.title: Crypto's $245 million campaign finance operation filled airwaves with ads not about crypto

facts.claim: In the 2024 cycle, Fairshake and its affiliated PACs were funded mainly by crypto companies. Coinbase gave more than $75 million, and Ripple Labs and Andreessen Horowitz were among the other primary contributors.

sources.title: How tech bros bought 'America's most pro-crypto Congress ever'

facts.claim: FEC data compiled by ProPublica's FEC Itemizer show Fairshake (committee C00835959) reported total receipts of $174,352,256 and total spending of $176,921,917 for the 2024 cycle through December 31, 2024. FactCheck.org puts Fairshake's total 2024-cycle spending at about $195.8 million, including more than $86 million it gave to its affiliates Defend American Jobs and Protect Progress. The two totals are computed on different bases and differ.
facts.quote: Fairshake spent about $195.8 million in total during the 2024 elections. It donated more than $86 million to Defend American Jobs and Protect Progress.

facts.claim: Fairshake operates with two affiliated super PACs: Defend American Jobs, which spends in Republican primaries, and Protect Progress, which spends in Democratic primaries. FactCheck.org identifies Coinbase, Ripple Labs and AH Capital Management (Andreessen Horowitz) as its largest contributors, and says a16z co-founders Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz remain two of its biggest individual donors.
facts.quote: Fairshake comprises three affiliated super PACs: Fairshake; Defend American Jobs, which spends in Republican primaries; and Protect Progress, which spends in Democratic primaries.

facts.claim: Wikipedia, citing FEC data, lists Fairshake's largest contributors since its 2023 founding as Coinbase ($93.5 million), Ripple Labs ($45 million), Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz ($33.5 million each) and Jump Trading ($25 million). These totals span more than one election cycle and should be checked against FEC filings before use.

facts.claim: In late May 2024 Ripple and Andreessen Horowitz each gave Fairshake $25 million, and in early June 2024 Coinbase gave a further $25 million, days after President Biden vetoed a congressional resolution on crypto custody accounting.

facts.claim: The Washington Post reported during the 2024 cycle that none of the Fairshake-network ads it viewed mentioned crypto, and that the super PACs were backed by Coinbase and Ripple. Inc. reported that Fairshake spent more than $10 million on television ads to defeat Rep. Katie Porter in California's Senate primary and that the ads did not mention crypto; Axios first reported the Porter ad campaign on February 28, 2024. CNBC described the network's ads as typically less about a candidate's support for or opposition to crypto and more about broader issues such as fairness and integrity.
facts.quote: none of the ads viewed by The Post actually mention crypto

facts.claim: FactCheck.org puts Defend American Jobs' 2024 spending supporting Bernie Moreno against Senator Sherrod Brown in Ohio at $40.1 million. The Hill, citing FEC records, puts the Fairshake network's total at about $41 million to oppose Brown and support Moreno, and describes Brown as having been seen as standing in the way of long-sought crypto legislation as head of the Senate Banking Committee.
facts.quote: In the 2024 cycle, Fairshake's affiliate Defend American Jobs spent $40.1 million supporting Bernie Moreno against Sherrod Brown in the Ohio Senate race.

sources.title: Fairshake
Sherrod Brown's quest for Senate comeback faces challenge from crypto industry

facts.claim: In September 2026 CoinDesk reported that Fairshake had devoted some $30 million to opposing former Senator Sherrod Brown's bid to return to the Senate from Ohio, with ads that do not mention crypto as an issue. Its affiliate Defend American Jobs reported to the FEC $11.4 million in media spending supporting Jon Husted and opposing Brown. Signal Akron reported that neither ad mentioned cryptocurrency: one promoted Husted and the other attacked Brown over past votes on the gas tax and the IRS.

facts.claim: On November 4, 2024 Fairshake said it had raised $78 million for the 2026 midterms, including new commitments from Coinbase and Andreessen Horowitz; Bloomberg reported a16z pledged $23 million. In January 2025 CNBC reported Fairshake had $116 million on hand for the 2026 elections. In early 2026 Fairshake reported a $193 million war chest ahead of the January 31 FEC deadline, with $25 million from Ripple and $24 million from a16z attributed to the second half of 2025.

facts.claim: On April 9, 2025 the Senate confirmed Paul S. Atkins as a member of the Securities and Exchange Commission by a 52-44 vote (record vote 205), for a term running through June 5, 2026; President Trump had nominated him on January 20, 2025. He was sworn in as the SEC's 34th chairman on April 21, 2025. On October 7, 2025 the Senate confirmed him for a further term expiring June 5, 2031 by a 51-47 vote.

facts.claim: The GENIUS Act (S. 1582), which creates a federal framework for payment stablecoins, passed the Senate 68-30 on June 17, 2025 and the House 308-122 on July 17, 2025 without amendment. President Trump signed it on July 18, 2025 and it became Public Law 119-27. CoinDesk reported that Coinbase chief executive Brian Armstrong attended the White House signing ceremony with executives from Tether, Circle, Gemini, Kraken and Chainlink, and that Trump singled him out during his remarks.
facts.quote: The President signed into law S. 1582, the "Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins Act" or "GENIUS Act," which provides for the regulation of payment stablecoins.

facts.claim: On July 17, 2025 the House passed the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act (H.R. 3633) by 294-134 (roll call 199), with 78 Democrats voting in favor, and sent it to the Senate. The bill would give the CFTC jurisdiction over digital commodities and narrow the SEC's role over digital asset securities.

sources.title: Actions - H.R.3633 - 119th Congress (2025-2026): Digital Asset Market Clarity Act
Clarity Act Sails Through U.S. House of Representatives Ahead of GENIUS Vote

facts.claim: On September 15, 2026 the Senate voted 49-50 against invoking cloture on the motion to proceed to the Clarity Act (record vote 234), short of the 60 votes needed; Republicans Susan Collins, Josh Hawley and Jerry Moran joined Democrats in voting no, and Senator Thom Tillis switched his vote to no to allow a motion to reconsider. Decrypt and The Block reported six days later that Fairshake had committed $30 million against Sherrod Brown's Ohio Senate campaign, with spokesman Geoff Vetter confirming the figure; both outlets presented the commitment in the context of the bill's failure.

facts.claim: In July 2025, announcing that it had raised $109 million since the November 2024 elections, including $52 million in the first half of 2025, Fairshake said the House would consider both the GENIUS Act and the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, and its spokesman Josh Vlasto said: 'Congress needs to stop playing politics with crypto and finally pass responsible regulation.' In January 2026 Vlasto said the group was continuing to oppose anti-crypto politicians and support pro-crypto leaders.
facts.quote: Congress needs to stop playing politics with crypto and finally pass responsible regulation

facts.claim: Testifying to the Senate Banking Committee on July 9, 2025, Ripple chief executive Brad Garlinghouse said: 'For the last decade, the legal and regulatory uncertainty surrounding crypto has prohibited meaningful progress in the U.S.', and argued in his submitted testimony that market structure legislation would catalyze a new era of U.S. competitiveness. In January 2026 he said the GENIUS Act had 'unlocked a lot of activity'.

facts.claim: In CoinDesk's July 17, 2025 round-up of reactions to the House votes, Mark Hays of Americans for Financial Reform, a group critical of the bills, said that the crypto industry's political spending was very close to securing a light-touch regulatory framework; Chuck Bell of Consumer Reports said the GENIUS Act does not provide the safeguards consumers reasonably expect. Industry figures quoted included Circle's Dante Disparte and Crypto Council for Innovation chief executive Ji Hun Kim, who called the GENIUS Act's passage a watershed moment.
facts.quote: the crypto industry's profligate political spending is very close to securing a light-touch regulatory framework

openQuestions: 'Deliberately concealing cryptocurrency': no source states intent. What reporters said is that the ads did not mention crypto (Washington Post: none of the ads it viewed mentioned crypto; Inc.: the Porter ads did not mention crypto; Signal Akron: neither 2026 Ohio ad mentioned cryptocurrency; CoinDesk: the 2026 Brown ads do not mention crypto as an issue) and that they ran on other themes (CNBC: fairness and integrity; Signal: gas tax and IRS votes; a New York Times article, as cited by the Citation Needed newsletter, said one ad focused on IRS agents and Social Security). A Fairshake spokesperson was reported as saying the Porter ads aimed to reach California crypto owners and highlight her stance on technology; that passage was not tied to a URL and is not recorded.

'Immunity for legacy operators': no source states this. Nearest sourced facts: Bankman-Fried was convicted and sentenced to 25 years; Singh, Salame, Ellison and Wang pleaded guilty; the SEC obtained final consent judgments against Ellison, Wang and Singh in December 2025 (see ftx.json).

'$260M+': no single sourced figure matches. Sourced figures are FEC receipts of $174.4 million for the 2024 cycle (ProPublica), $195.8 million spent in 2024 (FactCheck.org), $78 million raised for 2026 by November 2024, $116 million on hand in January 2025 and $193 million on hand in January 2026. A running total across cycles was not computed from a source.

The Wikipedia donor totals (Coinbase $93.5M, Ripple $45M, Andreessen and Horowitz $33.5M each) need checking against FEC receipts; the existing a16z finding records $67 million from AH Capital Management (Oct 2023 to Nov 2024) plus $23.8 million in December 2025.

Katie Porter was a House member running in a Senate primary, not a regulator or committee chair, so the brief's 'hostile regulators and committee chairs' applies only to Sherrod Brown (Senate Banking Committee chair) among the two named targets.

Fairshake's October 2026 list of House candidates it will spend for (CoinDesk, 2026-10-05) and FactCheck.org's August 2026 profile were in results but their passages were not captured; the latest 2026 cash-on-hand figure after January 2026 was not found.

'Securing pro-industry SEC leadership': no source gathered states a causal link between Fairshake spending and Paul Atkins's confirmation, the GENIUS Act or the Clarity Act's House passage. The one sourced statement tying industry political spending to the legislation is from a critic, Americans for Financial Reform's Mark Hays, in CoinDesk's July 17, 2025 round-up. No statement from Fairshake, Brian Armstrong or Brad Garlinghouse dated to the July 17-18, 2025 votes or signing was found; Armstrong's attendance at the signing is recorded. The SEC's February 2025 Coinbase dismissal and the 2025 end of the Ripple case are recorded in coinbase.json and ripple.json.

The GENIUS Act vote tallies (68-30 Senate, 308-122 House) and the Clarity Act tallies (294-134 House, 49-50 Senate cloture) are taken from Congress.gov action records as returned in search results; the owner may wish to confirm them on the roll-call pages.

Whether Fairshake or its donors issued statements on the Clarity Act's September 15, 2026 Senate failure was not established; the only Fairshake voice found afterwards is spokesman Geoff Vetter confirming the $30 million Ohio commitment.
